sources.role: official documentation; states source is not publicly available

paths.path: No persistent MG-Linux configuration file. Configure each launch with documented command-line options and the runtime F5 menu.
paths.naming: MG 4.9 -help defines hardware/language, timing, audio, video, SRAM/EEPROM, scaling, synchronization, and other flags; no profile-file argument or file grammar is exposed.
evidence: artifact:MG 4.9 Linux binary -help from MG49-Ubuntu-x86-bin.tgz sha256 25c8a0de
runtime:isolated MG 4.9 Linux test-ROM file trace opened only the ROM and its .sav/.sta sidecars; no HOME/XDG config path

paths.path: Runtime keyboard input with the fixed MG 4.9 bindings; no persistent MG-Linux controller profile.
paths.naming: Arrows are directions; Space/Shift/A/S/D/F/G/H/J/K/L/Q/E/T/U/O are FIRE-A, Control/Z/X/C/V/B/N/M/W/R/Y/I/P are FIRE-B, Enter is GameGear START, Tab is MasterSystem PAUSE, and Alt switches to controller 2. The official Linux binary/help does not expose a joystick selector or remapping grammar.
evidence: artifact:MG 4.9 Linux binary -help from MG49-Ubuntu-x86-bin.tgz sha256 25c8a0de

paths.path: <cartridge directory>/<cartridge basename>.sav for cartridge save memory.
paths.naming: .sav sidecar beside the cartridge; cartridge-dependent. An isolated absolute-path launch of test.sms probed test.sav in the same media directory.
evidence: runtime:isolated MG 4.9 Linux absolute-path test-ROM trace

paths.path: <cartridge directory>/<cartridge basename>.sta; loaded automatically on the next launch of that cartridge.
paths.naming: F7 saves and F6 loads the single cartridge-basename .STA state; cross-hardware/version compatibility is not guaranteed. An isolated absolute-path launch of test.sms probed test.sta beside the cartridge.
evidence: runtime:isolated MG 4.9 Linux absolute-path test-ROM trace

paths.path: <working directory>/SF7000.ROM only for SF7000 disk mode; no universal Sega BIOS.
paths.naming: Exactly 8 KiB SF7000.ROM; ordinary MasterSystem/GameGear/SG1000/SC3000 cartridge modes do not have a documented external BIOS requirement.

MG-Windows stores DWORD/string settings in the registry rather than an INI. A clean isolated launch wrote Mode, UPeriod, UseSound, VideoType and, after opening the F5 setup panel, BackSnd, Effects, Filename, FullScreen, Height, SaveCPU, SndDelay, SndRate, Width, X, Y and controller fields.

paths.path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\EMUL8\MG values DIJoystick0..DIJoystick3 and BtnEXIT/FIREA/FIREB/FIREL/FIRER/SELECT/START for players 1 and 2.
paths.naming: DWORD values. MG 4.6 documents saving physical joystick/gamepad selection, while the setup panel writes DIJoystick0..3 and button bitmasks; these are DirectInput/runtime device selections, not stable cross-host identities.
evidence: artifact:MG.exe 4.9 unpacked string table (DIJoystick%d and joystick setup labels)
runtime:isolated clean-prefix MG-Windows 4.9 F5 setup registry oracle

paths.naming: Cartridge basename with a .sav suffix beside the cartridge; cartridge-dependent SRAM/EEPROM persistence.
evidence: runtime:MG 4.9 Linux absolute-path sidecar trace corroborates shared core naming

paths.naming: F7 saves and F6 loads the single cartridge-basename .STA state automatically used on the next launch; version/hardware compatibility is not guaranteed.
evidence: runtime:MG 4.9 Linux absolute-path sidecar trace corroborates shared core path behavior

paths.path: <working directory>\SF7000.ROM only for SF7000 disk mode; no universal Sega BIOS.
paths.naming: Exactly 8 KiB SF7000.ROM; other supported cartridge modes have no documented external BIOS requirement.

notes: The official 4.9 binaries establish Linux command-line/fixed-keyboard behavior and the MG-Windows registry layout. A native controller writer remains intentionally absent because MG-Windows persists DirectInput/runtime enumeration selections rather than stable physical-device identities; official MasterGear source is unavailable. The isolated binary runs establish path behavior, not gameplay compatibility.
